task: Add a ServiceNow budget integration to the CodeMie backend: two service-account-only endpoints that resolve or create a project and cost center, assign project admins, and set, adjust or cancel the project's budget group, with authenticate() limiting the service account to those routes.

key_reasoning.reason: Base L. Adds four components (integration router, request/response models, orchestration service, scoped security module) that compose ProjectService, CostCenterService, ProjectAssignmentService and ProjectBudgetService, plus two extractions and two repository queries. The work spans the project, cost-center, membership and budget subsystems. Bumped to XL because it changes the shared authenticate() dependency.

The closest pattern is the Teams service account (TEAMS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID with teams_authentication_resolver). It identifies a service account but does not scope one to particular routes. The per-route allowlist reads request.scope['route'], which no source module uses today, so that gap counts as a security divergence. The service account bypasses maintainer_access_only and gets maintainer-level budget authority, with the allowlist as the only containment. The orchestration spans a sync Session and then an AsyncSession. A concurrent group create raises IntegrityError from a partial unique index, not the 409 the plan catches. LiteLLM sync runs before commit, so a rolled-back create can leave provider-side budgets behind. Base M, then two bumps to XL (security-pattern gap, authentication/authorization).

4 new source files and 7 modified source files (config.py, main.py, authentication.py, project_service.py, cost_center_service.py, user_repository.py, application_repository.py). About 8 test files, plus router-guard guarded_app.py and the regenerated openapi.json and route_precedence.json baselines. That covers the routers, security, service, repository, config and tests directories.

API (new router), Service (new orchestrator and extractions in existing services), DB-Persistence (new repository queries, no schema change), Infrastructure (config settings and main.py router wiring), and auth as a cross-cutting concern. No UI and no new outbound external client, so L, not XL.

An approved spec and plan exist and their anchors match source, apart from one stale validator-reference count. Some behaviour is still unspecified: the implicit dependency on ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT, IntegrityError handling on a concurrent group create, and passing through the stored mixed-case project name for the case-sensitive eligibility check. Scored M.
